newsitem.title: INDIA: Scan finds suspected spot on Mother Teresa's brain.
newsitem.headline: Scan finds suspected spot on Mother Teresa's brain.

text.p: A suspected spot has been detected on Mother Teresa's brain after the 86-year-old Roman Catholic missionary fell while getting out of bed and hit her head, a doctor said on Tuesday.

"We have detected a suspected spot in the initial scan report and we are awaiting a detailed report," Dr A.K. Bardhan of Woodlands Nursing Home in the eastern Indian city of Calcutta told Reuters. He said the revered nun was in stable condition.

Mother Teresa was admitted to the hospital's intensive coronary care unit on Monday after she suffered an injury above her right eye in a fall. After she was admitted to hospital, doctors said her condition was stable.
Mother Teresa, known as the Saint of the Gutters for her devotion to the poor and destitute, was in the same hospital between August 20 and September 6 with heart trouble, malaria and pneumonia.

"Her condition is stable but we are going to observe her for some more days," said Bardhan, the hospital's leading heart expert. He said the missionary did not want to remain in hospital, "but this time we are not releasing her immediately".
Bardhan said the hospital had asked a senior neurologist to examine Mother Teresa later on Tuesday.
